priority_review.rationale: Benign identity mentions can attract false positives. Before the model assigns priority review to this slice, require its observed per-label precision to meet the same 0.95 selection target at or above the population threshold. Rows that do not qualify can still enter ordinary human review or be escalated by a high-risk rule. This does not certify fairness or test-set precision, and it never permits automatic action.

rules.description: Threat predictions with p_threat >= 0.30 receive priority human review because missing a threat can be costly. This is a high-risk exception to the confidence target, not a claim of 95% precision. A reviewer confirms the case before any moderation action.

severe_toxic is a subset of toxic in the observed training labels: no row has severe_toxic=1 with toxic=0. Independently fitted heads can violate this relation. Escalate such predictions for priority human review; the inconsistency alone does not establish distribution shift or authorize moderation without confirmation.

retired_rules.was: identity_term_present == 1 AND p_max < 0.95 -> human_review, meant to suppress auto-action on borderline identity mentions.
retired_rules.why: Measured on the threshold-selection split (31,914 rows). From run 20260922T100649877069Z, made with the rule still active: the auto-action thresholds chosen from the 0.99 floor were 0.989 (toxic), 0.998 (obscene) and 0.9998 (insult), all above the rule's 0.95 band, so the rule could never intercept an auto-action, and because rules override the model tier in both directions its only effect was to move 1,825 allow-tier comments with an identity term into the human queue, of which 1,670 (92%) had no positive label, giving a queue precision of 0.404 and concentrating human scrutiny on the speech it meant to protect. From the run named in gates.eval_slice (same split, same population thresholds, rule removed): the premise check on the population tier (classifier alone, false positive per each tier's own definition), where the false discovery rate among predicted positives was 0.071 with an identity term (15 of 210) and 0.068 without (128 of 1,869), ratio 1.04, 95% interval 0.62 to 1.75: neither confirmed nor excluded for that FDR comparison. It does not establish parity in FPR among truly negative comments. Two replacements were considered. An unconditional cap (identity mentions never auto-actioned) would have turned all 102 identity-term auto-action rows on that split, every one truly positive by some label, into human reviews to prevent about two wrong-trigger enforcements; rejected as a blunt override of the floor-defined tiers. Instead the floor is required on the slice itself (subgroup_thresholds above) and the concentration is measured and gated on every run.

gates.eval_slice: Classification references use the unchanged classifier heads: clean run 20260922T112845423138Z-baseline at commit 3429f1fe41701d31de68ac936530d6aebfee1132 supplies AP; feature-branch run 20260922T131021772191Z-baseline on a dirty worktree supplies the human operating-point precision and volume diagnostics. V2 human-review routing was measured separately in 20260922T130141204182Z-human-review-baseline on a dirty worktree. The v2 no-worse-FIFO criteria were declared before that run. The absolute capacity limits below are adopted before the new merged v2 run and are not measurements or fitted tolerances from that run.

rules.note: rule-forced queue entries are included in every tier and simulation metric

prevalence_shift.definition: volume_overshoot = model-expected positives (sum of calibrated p on the test rows) / actual positives - 1; prevalence ratio = training-file prevalence / test prevalence

assumptions.arrivals: Post-admission Poisson review arrivals; jobs sampled with replacement from the combined priority_review and human_review pool
assumptions.arrival_rates_are: post-admission review demand, not all incoming comments
assumptions.priority_order: priority_review first, then human_review; within each tier, higher max predicted probability times severity weight first; ties use arrival order
assumptions.review_completion_definition: simulated reviewer service finished; moderation requires human confirmation; no enforcement outcome is observed
assumptions.wait_definition: start of review minus arrival, over jobs that started (completed or in progress); never-started jobs are counted, not timed
assumptions.completion_latency_definition: completion minus arrival, over jobs completed within the horizon
assumptions.harm_proxy: max severity weight over TRUE labels (0 if clean); not real-world harm
assumptions.per_job_records: simulation_jobs.csv in the run directory; every time metric here is recomputable from it

headline.population: jobs that started, including in-progress reviews; pooled over seeds; populations may differ by strategy; read with completion and unfinished counts

supplementary_high_risk.note: reported alongside, never a substitute for the selected metric

primary.note: queue-clearing gates read this load; the router strategy is compared against fifo at the same load for time-to-action

thesis.note: harm handled per reviewer-hour only differs between orderings when the queue does not clear, so the FIFO comparison reads this load

threshold_selection.definition: identity term = any whole-word match of review_router.signals.IDENTITY_TERMS; predicted positive = routed to priority_review or human_review; false positive = no ground-truth label is positive, for both review tiers; FDR = false positives / predicted positives; FDR ratio = with-term FDR / without-term FDR with a 95% log-ratio interval. clean_negative_false_positives separately reports FPR = clean comments routed to the tier / all clean comments in that subgroup. allow_false_omission = truly positive allowed comments / all allowed comments.

test.definition: identity term = any whole-word match of review_router.signals.IDENTITY_TERMS; predicted positive = routed to priority_review or human_review; false positive = no ground-truth label is positive, for both review tiers; FDR = false positives / predicted positives; FDR ratio = with-term FDR / without-term FDR with a 95% log-ratio interval. clean_negative_false_positives separately reports FPR = clean comments routed to the tier / all clean comments in that subgroup. allow_false_omission = truly positive allowed comments / all allowed comments.
